user.title: LoadCast
user.description: LoadCast learns your household's consumption from recorder history and forecasts the next 24–48 hours. First choose how total consumption is measured.

sensor.title: Total consumption sensor
sensor.description: A sensor measuring the whole household's consumption: an energy sensor (kWh, total increasing) or a power sensor (W). It needs long-term statistics.

computed.title: Compute consumption from energy flows
computed.description: Consumption = grid import − grid export + solar + battery discharge − battery charge. Leave out what you don't have.

temperature.title: Temperature (optional)
temperature.description: With an outdoor temperature sensor LoadCast learns how consumption depends on temperature, and with a weather entity it uses the hourly forecast for future hours.

add_subload.title: Add sub-load
add_subload.description: A separately metered load (heat pump, EV charger, pool …) gets its own model, so a change in it – such as a heat pump failing – is learned within days. Untick 'include in total' for loads another automation plans itself (typically EV charging).

settings.title: Model settings
settings.description: The history window is how many days the model looks back. How much each day counts is chosen by the model itself from outcomes.

options.computed: Compute from grid, solar and battery

get_forecast.name: Get forecast
get_forecast.description: Forecast household consumption between two times.

components.name: Components
components.description: Only these components (e.g. base, Heat pump). Default: the total.

mark_change.name: Mark a change
mark_change.description: A component's consumption changed for a known reason (a heat pump repaired or replaced, a new appliance). LoadCast forgets that component's history before the change and relearns from the new level. Until it has a day of new data the forecast reports ready=false.

component.name: Component
component.description: 'base' or the name of a sub-load, e.g. Heat pump.

since.name: Since
since.description: When the change happened. Default: now.
